label: Exposed "colonial feminism" as imperial weaponization of the veil
description: Extending Fanon's analysis of colonial unveiling strategy in "Algeria Unveiled," Leila Ahmed showed how Lord Cromer and British imperialism co-opted Western feminist rhetoric to justify colonial domination in Egypt.
dialecticalTension: Reveals how feminist slogans can function simultaneously as emancipation and imperial alibi.

citations.author: Leila Ahmed
citations.work: Women and Gender in Islam: Historical Roots of a Modern Debate

label: Reassessed early Egyptian feminism's entanglement with Westernizing elites
description: Leila Ahmed traced Huda Sha'arawi's Egyptian Feminist Union to show both its vital anti-colonial nationalism and the class-bound Westernizing assumptions that alienated subaltern piety movements.
dialecticalTension: Balances appreciation of civic suffrage struggles against critique of Eurocentric modernity.
historicalContext: Chapter 9 of Women and Gender in Islam (1992).

label: Grounded historical genealogy of modern Muslim piety and re-veiling
description: Ahmed's historical demonstration that Islamic revivalism and veiling carried non-colonial civic meanings directly informed Saba Mahmood's anthropological-philosophical study of Cairo's mosque movement.
dialecticalTension: Bridges historical intellectual genealogy with ethnographic theory of moral agency.
